Daeun Choi

M.S. student in Mechanical Engineering, AMS Lab

Sookmyung Women's University. Advisor: Prof. Joo Yong Sim.

I build wearable suits that assist human movement with shape memory alloys, from hardware and modeling to control.

In a PhD, I want to study personalized soft exosuits that learn from each wearer’s movement and muscle activity, combining physics-based models with learning so that assistance adapts quickly and works reliably in daily life.

Research

My research asks what it takes to turn light, silent SMA actuators into assistive devices people can actually wear. Each entry below is one paper or presentation, with a key figure and a short summary.

Motion-Aware Model Predictive Control of a Self-Sensing Woven SMA Lumbar Assist Suit to Overcome Thermal Response Delay

Daeun Choi, Joo Yong Sim†
In progress · M.S. research, AMS Lab

SMA produces force only after heating, and that thermal delay limits fast assistance. An MPC built on an SMA force model over displacement and temperature, F = f(x, T), predicts force and temperature and heats the SMA ahead of the lift, so the assist force arrives when the wearer needs it. An EGaIn-based strain sensor is woven into the actuator, so temperature, displacement, and force can all be estimated from electrical sensor signals alone, without external devices.

3.43 Nforce tracking RMSE (3.8% of 90 N peak)
1.05 °Ctemperature prediction RMSE (0.9% of 120 °C peak)
28.4%lower muscle activity vs. unassisted
32.2%lower muscle activity vs. no suit

Modular Shape Memory Alloy Linear Actuator Driven Elbow Exoskeleton with Geometry-Based Passive Cooling Design and Performance Assessment

Junhwan Choi*, Daeun Choi*, Minji Jeon, Se-Eun Lee, Chae-eun Shin, Woosung Park, Jung Kim, Youngjin Na†, Joo Yong Sim† *Equal contribution, †Co-corresponding
Published · Scientific Reports, 2026 (article in press)

A hexagonal arrangement of SMA wires shortens the cooling time constant, and modules connect in parallel or series to scale force and stroke. In a cable-driven elbow exoskeleton, biceps EMG from 17 subjects showed significantly lower muscle activity.

My role Co-first author. Actuator design and characterization, current control, force and displacement experiments, and co-writing.

41.2 Npeak force per module
35–50%shorter cooling time constant
13.2–44.7%lower muscle activity, n = 17
Presentations
Oral

Woven Shape Memory Alloy Actuator for Intelligent Back Assistive Wearable Suit

Daeun Choi, Se-Eun Lee, Joo Yong Sim†
KSME Annual Conference, Dec 2025 · prototype of the ongoing work

Inspired by muscle fibers, the actuator plain-weaves SMA coils with silicone tubes, which dissipate heat and enable faster cooling. In a back-assist suit with three IMUs, the hip angle estimates knee and ankle angles, posture is classified into four states, and the SMA is pre-heated before a lift. The ongoing work builds on this prototype: a deep-learning posture detector replaces MediaPipe-based estimation, an MPC controller is added, and a woven EGaIn strain sensor is integrated.

Awards and competitions

Each award with its certificate, a photo from the event, and my role. Certificates are issued in Korean; English names are given in the text.

Outstanding Thesis Award

Undergraduate Thesis, School of Mechanical Systems Engineering

Jan 2026 · Sookmyung Women's University

For Woven Shape Memory Alloy Actuator for Intelligent Back Assistive Wearable Suit, recognized for originality and quality of research.

Highlight

Sensorless temperature estimation: SMA temperature predicted from input power alone with a physics model plus learned residual correction, so the suit needs no thermocouple.

Result

RMSE 1.15 °C in the isometric test and RMSE 0.96 °C in the isotonic test, tracking measured temperature more closely than the physics model alone.

Excellence Award

5th X-Corps Plus Festival

Nov 2025 · National Research Foundation of Korea · Team Texturing (4 members)

Demonstrated a working back-assist suit prototype with a textile SMA actuator, and a real-time interface that shows assist force and renders the wearer's posture as a 3D SMPL human body model as they lift.

Role

Fabricated the textile SMA actuator, integrated the load cell and IMU sensors, connected them to the real-time UI, and designed and presented the poster.

Learned

Carrying a real-world problem from requirements to a demonstrable prototype, and integrating actuation, sensing, and visualization into one system.

Honorable Mention (7th place)

4th F1TENTH Korea Championship

Nov 2025 · Kookmin University Future Vehicle Innovation Program · Team GROMIT (8 members)

1/10-scale autonomous racing on a track with obstacle zones and head-to-head runs.

Role

Built the car's localization. I implemented a Kalman filter that fuses IMU measurements with wheel odometry to estimate the car's position and heading in real time, filtering out sensor noise and drift so the planner and controller could rely on a stable pose.

Learned

State estimation under noisy sensors and real-time limits. It is the same problem as estimating SMA temperature without a sensor: infer a hidden state from what you can measure.

Silver Award

4th MEIT Major Convergence Project Competition

Oct 2025 · Sookmyung Women's University · Team Chaeum

A compact sanitary pad dispenser. A single motor drives a slider-crank mechanism that pushes out one pad per cycle within a tight enclosure. Users tap an RFID card to dispense, and sensors track stock, with the remaining count shown on a display.

Role

Led the hardware team, from mechanism design and sensor integration through to communication with the UI.

Learned

Getting the motion you need from one actuator through mechanism design, the same constraint I face in compact wearable devices.

Activities
  • Learning Community, Sookmyung Women's University, 2025. Studied memory management through Wilson's survey of garbage collection (1992), focusing on the trade-off between throughput and pause time. I relate it to deploying my controller and ML models on the suit's microcontroller, where memory footprint and predictable latency matter.
  • Rndix, student AI study group, 2026 (ongoing).
    • Physical AI: learning robot simulation with NVIDIA Isaac Sim, after covering robot kinematics (rotations, SE(3), forward and inverse kinematics, Jacobians), scripted-policy demonstration collection, and robot-learning datasets. I aim to use simulation for suit personalization and learning-based control, and for sim-to-real transfer: testing suit controllers, such as my MPC, on a human and suit model before running human experiments.
    • Efficient AI: following Prof. Song Han's MIT course on efficient deep learning (model compression and on-device inference). I aim to apply it to running my IMU motion classifier and sensorless temperature estimator within the memory and compute limits of the suit's embedded hardware.
Technical skills
  • Hardware and fabrication: SMA actuator design and fabrication (modular linear, woven textile), PCB design and fabrication (SMA current driver), wearable suit integration, textile sensors (silver-thread temperature, EGaIn strain)
  • Sensing and embedded: IMU, load cell, surface EMG, thermocouple, ESP32, RS485
  • Control and estimation: PID, model predictive control, Kalman filter
  • Machine learning: Bi-LSTM motion classification, Random Forest and gradient boosting regression, pose estimation (MediaPipe, 4D-Humans, SMPL)
  • Experiments: force and thermal characterization (force gauge, FLIR), human-subject EMG testing
